newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle end higher as corn futures fall.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle end higher as corn futures fall.

text.p: CME feeder cattle futures surged to higher closes, buoyed by lower corn futures, ideas that feeder cattle prices will seasonally trend higher into the fall and on fund buying, traders said. Live cattle followed despite a weak June expiration, traders said.

Feeder cattle closed 1.175 to 0.300 cent per lb higher, paced by August at 78.475 cents. Live cattle ended 0.700 to 0.325 cent a lb higher with August up 0.500 at 63.950 cents. June expired earlier at 64.700, off 0.500 on the day.

"Seasonals are overwhelmingly in favor of buying feeders right now," said Steve Morgan with Commodity Review and Outlook. "From now through about the first week in August, August feeder cattle have rallied 14 of the last 15 years."
Morgan noted that feeder supplies are tight and the industry is looking ahead to lower feed costs once corn and soy crops are harvested, which would encourage demand for feeder futures.
The latest CME feeder cattle index slipped $0.02 to $78.01 per cwt, but is still at the highest level since August 1994.

FIMAT Futures USA, Cargill Investor Services, Dean Witter, Iowa Grain and ABN Chicogo Corp bought August, traders said, and Cargill also spread long February live cattle/short August feeders, long June 1998 cattle/short January feeders and long April cattle/short November feeders. Commission houses bought October 68 and 70 puts late in options, pit sources said.

Live cattle generally followed the lead of feeder cattle and Rand Financials up for gains with October through February pacing the advance. Short covering supported nearbys early but late long liquidation in June ahead of expiration weighed on those months, traders said.

Demand in live cattle came despite apparent topping in wholesale boxed beef prices and lower packer bids for fed cattle to start the week. Seasonal beef demand is seen declining during the summer and packers have more than adequate contract cattle available ahead, they added.

Refco, Cargill and E.D.&F. Man bought August while RBH and Term Commodities sold. In live cattle options, Cargill Investor Services sold August 64 calls. Refco sold the December put spread, buying 70 puts and selling 66 puts, pit sources said.
